conversations.title: 'I turned to online dating to find love of my life - but it's vile and exhausting'
conversations.reply: Phoebe's experience with online dating is heartbreaking, and it's shocking that she's had to deal with so many rude messages about her sex life just because she's in a wheelchair. She deserves so much better.

conversations.title: Disability Pride Month & The Black Queer Disabled Voices Shaping Culture
conversations.reply: It's amazing to see Jay and Pamela using their platform to speak openly about their queer identity and disability, and it's fantastic that they're helping to shape culture and promote visibility and representation.

conversations.title: On the inaccessible built environment
conversations.reply: Carly Findlay's post really highlights the everyday barriers that people face, and it's frustrating that accessibility is still an afterthought for so many architects and designers.

conversations.title: UK Pubs and Clubs Get Tax Cuts. Hotels Get Left Out ,  Again
conversations.reply: It's interesting that pubs and clubs are getting tax cuts, and maybe this is an opportunity for hotels to think about how they can be more inclusive and appealing to a wider range of customers.

conversations.title: Norwich City Hall upgrade to include disabled access ramp
conversations.reply: The new access ramp at Norwich City Hall is a really positive move, showing that the council is serious about making the building more accessible to everyone. This upgrade will make a big difference to people who visit or work there.

conversations.title: Why the 'no wristband, no service' policy at Manchester Village Pride this year is a defiant choice
conversations.reply: Glad Manchester Village Pride is thinking about safety and inclusivity, hope it works out for everyone.

conversations.title: Inclusion + Accessibility Specialist (@shanidhanda)
conversations.reply: Shani Dhanda's work on inclusion and accessibility is fantastic, and it's great to see her using her platform to promote disability pride and awareness.

conversations.title: Dr Shani Dhanda is an Influencer Multi-Award-Winning Disability Inclusion & Accessibility Consultant
conversations.reply: Shani Dhanda is doing amazing work, and it's fantastic to see her being recognized for her efforts to promote disability inclusion and accessibility.

Task: today's Able2Love engagement round (2026-08-04). You are working in my logged-in browser as the app's accounts: @Able2LoveApp on X, @able2loveapp on Instagram.

APPROVAL RULE, NEVER BREAK IT: before posting anything, show me the post you found and your drafted reply, and wait for my yes. Never post without a yes for that specific item. If I say no or skip, find a replacement candidate so we still hit today's targets.

TARGETS: 10 replies on X and 5 comments on Instagram, found and posted a few at a time (pause whenever I say pause). Skip and tell me if we run out of genuinely good candidates; never pad with weak ones.

FINDING CANDIDATES:
- X: use x.com search (Latest tab) for: disability dating, dating with a disability, accessible venue, wheelchair nightlife, #DisabilityDating, #DisabledAndDating, chronic illness dating, plus anything matching today's ammo below. Real people only: skip news outlets, brands, giveaways, and anything about death, grief, tragedy or self-harm.
- Instagram: work through the hit-list below (hashtag pages and creator types), picking recent posts where a comment genuinely fits.

VOICE, NON-NEGOTIABLE: write from the Able2Love account like a real person who built it and cares, warm and on the poster's side. React to what each post actually is: agree and back people up when they've had a rough time, help when they ask, be glad for them when they celebrate. You HAVE an opinion, warm agreement not cold analysis, all tracing back to one belief: the way disabled daters get treated on the big apps is wrong and this app is changing it. Usually 1 to 2 short sentences on X, shorter is fine for IG. UK English. NEVER use an em dash or en dash. Disability is never the punchline. Never invent facts, studies, numbers, or claims about any venue, person, company, or the app's features. Never argue; skip hostile threads. Never preachy or lecturing: no "access should be the baseline", "legal requirement", "not a favour", "stark reminder", "raising awareness", "it's time to". Never negative at the person. Every reply a different shape: never reuse a phrase across replies, never post the ammo lines verbatim.

- Shani Dhanda's work on inclusion and accessibility is fantastic, and it's great to see her using her platform to promote disability pride and awareness.
- Shani Dhanda is doing amazing work, and it's fantastic to see her being recognized for her efforts to promote disability inclusion and accessibility.
